description: API-shape experiment for drawing an audio clip's waveform inside an app-rendered timeline clip element, trimming clips by dragging their edges, and opening a clip in a detailed editor. Expectations describe behaviour, not names.

tasks.prompt: A browser DAW renders its own timeline: one row per track and one absolutely positioned `<div>` per clip, 40 px tall, placed from the clip's start and length (100 px per second). The song is `project` and its engine is `workspace`. Write the code that, for every audio clip element, (1) draws a small waveform of only the part of the recording the clip plays, filling the clip box, matching the page's light or dark theme, and (2) lets the user drag the clip's left or right edge to trim it, snapping to the nearest beat, without destroying audio: dragging the edge back out brings the cut audio back. Each trim is one Undo step, the waveform follows the trimmed window, and the clip body can still be dragged to move it. Keep it working when clips are added, removed or reloaded.
expectations: Draws each audio clip's waveform with a toolkit view sized to the clip element, without hand-drawing peaks on a canvas.
The waveform shows only the clip's played window of the recording and follows trims.
Edge dragging uses a toolkit gesture rather than hand-written pointer handling.
Trims snap to beats and commit through the song model as one Undo step each, non-destructively.
Moving the clip body still works alongside trimming.
Views and gestures are created and disposed as clips are added, removed or reloaded.

tasks.prompt: In the same browser DAW (`project`, `workspace`, an app-rendered timeline where `clipElement(clipId)` returns a clip's element), double-clicking an audio clip opens a detail editor below the timeline: it shows the whole recording the clip comes from as a zoomable waveform with the clip's current window selected, lets the user drag the selection to choose a different part and audition just that part, and has Apply and Cancel buttons. Apply sets the clip to play exactly the selected part of the recording, starting at the clip's current timeline position, as one Undo step; Cancel closes without changes. Closing the editor releases everything it created.
expectations: Shows the clip's whole source recording in a toolkit waveform view with selection and zoom, without hand-drawing.
The initial selection is the clip's current played window of the recording.
Auditions only the selected part through toolkit playback.
Apply sets the clip's played window to the selection at its current timeline position as one Undo step.
Cancel closes without changing the song.
Closing disposes the views and playback it created.
